Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public. 




Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan 
"The Right to Information, The Right to Live''

UDC 615-472 : [ 621-918'4] :619 IS : 12243 - 1988 



Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
RASP, TOOTH, REVERSIBLE 



( Reaffirmed 2006 ) 



1. Scope «• This standard covers requirements for a set of three pieces of tooth rasp, reversible, 
for veterinary use, 

2. Dimensions — Shall conform to Fig. 1 . 

24 The tolerance on dimensions of working ends shall conform to 'fine' class of deviation and the 
tolerance for remaining dimensions shall conform to 'medium'' class of deviation of IS : 21 02 
( Part 1 )-1980 'General tolerances for dimensions and form and position: Part 1 General toler- 
ances for linear and angular dimensions ( second revision )'. 

3* Materials — Shall conform to designation 11 8T3 of IS : 3749-1978 'Specification for tool 
and die steels for cold Vv'ork ( first revision )'. 

4. Manufacture, Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The surfaces of the rasps except for the tines and threads shall be smooth and free from 
pitting. The edges shall be even and rounded. The tines shall be well formed. The form and 
pitch of the threads shall be correct. The male part of rasp shall screw accurately into the 
female parts of rasp. The male rasp of one set shall fit accurately into the female rasps of any 
other set in the same supply and vice versa.. 

4.2 The surface of the working ends shall be free from all defects like burrs, pits, cracks, nicks 
and waviness when examined under x 10 magnification. All surfaces shall be free from pores, 
crevices and grinding marks. 

4.2.1 The rasps shall be supplied free from residual scales, acid, grease and grinding and 
polishing materials. Compliance with these requirements shall be checked under x 2 magnification. 

5* Hardness — Rasp shall be accurately and evenly hardened and tempered to give a hardness 
of 650 to 750 HV. 

6. Test — Each rasp piece shall be used for filing the teeth on a horse jaw bone continuously for 
two minutes. The rasp shall be able to do it easily. On completion of the test, the tines on the 
rasp shall not show any sign of wear. 

7- Surface Finish — The surface finish shall be mirror finish. The instrument should be 
adequately ground to remove all surface imperfections and polished to remove grinding marks, 
resulting in a mirror finish. The mirror finish should be effected by an appropriate procedure, such 
as polishing, brushing, electroplolishing and mirror buffing. 

8. Sampling — Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, the sampl- 
ing procedure given in IS : 2500 ( Part 1 )-1973 'Sampling inspection tables: Part 1 Inspection 
by attributes and by count of defects ( first revision )\ shall be followed. 

g.1 Lot — All tooth rasps of the same size, shape and belonging to the same batch of manufacture 
shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. 

8.2 For dimensions and requirements given in 2, 4 and 7, a single sampling plan with inspection 
level IV and AQL 4 percent given in Tables 1 and 2 of IS : 2500 ( Part 1 )-1973 shall be followed. 

8.3 For the requirement given in 5, a single sampling plan with inspection level I and AQL 1 per- 
cent given in Tables 1 and 2 of IS : 2500 ( Part 1 )-1973 shall be followed. 

9, Marking — Each rasp shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's nam.e, 
initials or recognized trade marks, 

9.1 Standard Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards.

FIG. 1 TOOTH RASP, REVERSIBLE 

10. Packing — The set of rasps shall be delivered in a new and clean condition free from all 
traces of rust. Each rasp shall be coated with a thin film of rust preventing solution and wrapped 
in normal waxed grade kraft paper. The rasp shall be packed in a set in leather case and tied 
with a strap The empty space, if any, shall be filled with suitable cushioning material to prevent 
movement. 

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

While preparing this standard assistance has been derived from Doc. No. IND/GS/MED/528 
( c ) Rasp, tooth, reversible, set of 3 pieces; issued by CQA ( GS ), Kanpur, Ministry of Defence.
